mappings.note: Rules kept in one's family and neighbourhood and why they matter - the socio-economic role of the family as an institution, which only the goal CG-SST4 states. CG-SST4's outcomes cover occupations, contacts abroad, culture and ancient thought, none of which reaches family norms.

Asks whether some family or community rules are unfair, with all housework falling on women as the example: recognising discrimination (LO-192) and telling inequality from equality (LO-193). Deliberately not CG-SST4, since the point is the unfairness, not the institution.
Observed cases where community support made a difference - the community acting as a social institution, so the goal. Not LO-191, since the item asks what the community DOES, not what forms it takes.
The family as society's oldest and most basic unit; CG-SST4 names the family among the institutions whose role pupils should grasp.
Defines the nuclear family - a form of the family institution, so the goal, with the joint-family items.
The absence of a word for 'cousin' read as evidence of close kinship bonds; the item's point is how the family binds its members, hence CG-SST4 rather than a language-diversity outcome.
Mutual interdependence as the basis of family relationships - the internal working of the institution.
Parents' responsibility to raise happy, well-adjusted children; a role within the family institution.

Dana as giving, learned in the family: the family as transmitter of values (CG-SST4) and dana itself as a value of India's older systems of thought (LO-200). The pure family-structure items take CG-SST4 alone.
Tyaga as sacrifice for others - the companion value item to dana, and mapped the same way.
Shalini accepting a plainer dress so her uncle's family could also have new clothes; family solidarity over individual preference, so CG-SST4.

Tenzing's father taking on household chores shows shared responsibility and flexible gender roles: the family's working (CG-SST4) and the equality question LO-193 raises. Distinguished from the items that only describe family structure.
The grandfather's social work for the colony - an individual's contribution to community welfare, which CG-SST4 covers as the contributions of different sections of society.
Parents discussing expenses and saving for the unexpected: the family's economic function, squarely the socio-economic role in CG-SST4.
Defines a community as connected families living close together - a form of human grouping around the pupil, which is LO-191. CG-SST4 is used where the item is about what the community DOES.
Why community members gather - festivals, feasts, weddings; the community's binding function rather than its varieties, so CG-SST4.
The Bhil halma tradition of collective help in a crisis - a named community's socio-economic support mechanism, hence CG-SST4.

Mahesh Sharma honoured for tree planting and water conservation through halma; an individual's contribution mobilising a community, which CG-SST4's 'contributions of different sections of society' covers.
Private groups feeding people during the 2015 Chennai floods - spontaneous community support, mapped with halma under CG-SST4. Not LO-194, since the point is that this was NOT government action.

Residents' associations relying on municipal workers for waste: the local government's role (LO-194) meeting a community institution (CG-SST4). This is the first item in the chapter where government proper enters.
Jati or its subdivisions counted as a 'community' in India - a form of human diversity in the pupil's own society, so LO-191.
Joint families spanning several generations against nuclear ones; a contrast of family forms, so CG-SST4.
Matches mausi to mother's sister among Hindi kinship terms - the fine-grained vocabulary of the Indian family, which belongs with the family institution.
Assertion that children learn dana by watching it practised at home: the family as teacher (CG-SST4) of a traditional value (LO-200), like the other dana item.
Statement set on grandparents' wisdom, parents' primary role and children's own responsibilities - the distribution of roles inside the family, so CG-SST4.
Neighbours fighting a barn fire and rebuilding unpaid; community cooperation as a social institution, so CG-SST4 with halma and the Chennai floods.
Defines cooperation as working together for a common purpose - the mechanism on which family and community life rests.
Halma as the response to individual or family crises; the same tradition as the earlier item, asked from the occasion rather than the action.

Kamal Parmar's evening pupils learning eagerly without benches or quiet - a volunteer's contribution to a community's children, which CG-SST4 covers. Not LO-196, since this is not a government body's education work.
Picks the 'scientific community' as the group formed by shared work, against religious, school and farming groupings - the item is about KINDS of community, so LO-191.
Cousins addressed as brothers and sisters; the kinship-bond point again, so CG-SST4 rather than a language outcome.
Joint families pooling resources against financial hardship - the family's economic role, which is the 'socio-economic' clause of CG-SST4.
Neighbours running cleanliness drives and tree planting; a community acting for its own welfare, hence CG-SST4 and not the government outcome.

Finds the false pairing by knowing what each community is formed around (LO-191) and that a Residents' Welfare Association is a local self-organised body, not an arm of the national government (LO-194).
A village granary built on compulsory contributions and used for the needy - collective responsibility and resource pooling, the socio-economic role of a community institution.
Tenzing's grandmother as the family's storyteller; a role within the family, so CG-SST4 with the other Tenzing items.
Rules out 'complete isolation' from what families provide, keeping love, values, care and cooperation - the family's functions, hence CG-SST4.
Locates Shalini's family in Kerala from the mention of Onam and the local kinship terms: regional diversity (LO-191) met through a family story (CG-SST4).
Unwritten community rules securing access to shared resources by setting duties - the community as a regulating institution, so CG-SST4. Not LO-194: no government is involved.
Identifies NSS and NCC in school as communities formed round shared activity, against halma, RWAs and tuition; the item is about what counts as a community, so LO-191.
